title: Ask the lesson's question first and last
statement: Ask the lesson's question at the start and again at the end, keeping both answers side by side and marking neither.
example: One lesson engine opens the question with two or three of its phrases explained, keeps a first answer unmarked, and saves the end-of-lesson answer beside it.
detail: An audit of the Grade 9 lesson engine found its export asked the lesson's question only as first thoughts, and proposed the bookends a 3D version draws: the question shown on its own with its key phrases explained, then answered again at the end (`g9-transformer-audit/2026-10-09-best-of-everything.json`). The learning-question block built on 9 October explains two or three phrases, and a judge checks that each note says what its phrase asks or means without answering the question. A first answer may be kept and is never marked; at the end the question is answered again and saved beside the first, also unmarked, and the judge may name what the second answer adds, in a line that quotes neither, only when it is sure (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/learning-question.js`).
against: The export to a 3D version leaves out the return at the end: "its return at the end of the lesson is a closing step, not exported" (`g9/transformer/src/glue/threejs-render.js`, line 234; `g9-transformer-audit/2026-10-09-builders.json`, line 1). The design comes from another build, and the sources give no measure of what the second answers add. The first answer is optional ("Code only: both answers are saved, never marked; the first is optional.", `g9/transformer/src/mechanics/learning-question.js`, line 89).
